subject: Post-call action map: reserved GPU scope & isolation requirements
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Bradley <sam@kardiahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call action map: reserved GPU scope & isolation requirements

Sam — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and the actions we discussed so your team can review: 

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Unpredictable latency during peak inference (5–10s tail on batch model) impacting user-facing workflows.
- Data isolation & compliance: PHI adjacency concerns require a dedicated, single-tenant pool for model serving.
- Cost sensitivity: need predictable per-hour cost for budgeting and procurement.

Goals we captured:
- Launch a pilot with 8 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs (or RTX 6000-equivalent if preferred) in a private VPC by Jan 15.
- Protect PHI via network isolation + customer-managed KMS and audit logs.
- Hit 99.9% availability SLA for inference endpoints and median token latencies under 150ms for short prompts.

Draft scope & sizing (high-level):
- Initial reserved pool: 8 GPUs (can start with 4 active + 4 warm standby for burst).
- MLP for autoscaling: burst to +50% with pre-approved credits; plan for horizontal scaling if utilization exceeds 70% sustained.
- KV cache and prefix caching recommended for your conversational traffic to lower token cost.

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA):
1) Ben: Share GPU sizing workbook and SLA draft (attached) — today.
2) Sam: Confirm whether A100 or RTX-class preferred and provide preferred maintenance window — by 12/03.
3) Rishi: Draft procurement/commercial term options (reserved monthly vs committed annual) — by 12/04.
4) Marissa: Align CS for onboarding runbook and 1-week canary checklist — by 12/07.

Attachments: redwood-sla-draft-v1.pdf, gpu-sizing-estimate.xlsx

If that matches your view, I’ll schedule a brief ops alignment call with your infra lead and our SRE on Thursday.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

---
Note: This is a summary for the internal and external stakeholders; the SLA draft is intentionally high level at this stage.

From: Sam Bradley <sam@kardiahealth.com>

Cc: Cleo Tan <cleo@novagen.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call action map: reserved GPU scope & isolation requirements

Ben — thanks, very helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

1) GPU class: we prefer A100 (40GB) for the first phase because our models use ~20–25k context and we want the KV cache headroom.
2) Availability SLA: 99.9% is acceptable, but we need an escalation path that includes a 30-minute hotfail fallback to a lower-cost multi-tenant endpoint if the dedicated pool is degraded.
3) Data security: we will require customer-managed keys and an audit log dump weekly during pilot. Can you confirm the log retention window?

We'll confirm the maintenance window and share an infra contact by EOD Friday. Also, we have procurement constraints — our finance team prefers a quarterly invoicing cadence if possible for the pilot.

Sam

Looping in ops and commercial context. A few notes: 

- Commercial: Ben, I’ll draft two commercial options — (A) 6-month pilot, monthly billing, limited burst credits; (B) 12-month committed with a 10% discount and quarterly invoices. I’ll put both in HubSpot and tag finance.
- Ops: For the hotfail fallback Sam requested, we can design a policy: automatic routing to a multi-tenant fallback model variant limited to read-only user flows, with QoS throttling. Will require a small traffic-splitting canary first.
- Security: KMS-managed keys + weekly audit export is feasible. Retention: we keep detailed auth/audit events for 90 days by default; we can extend to 365 days under enterprise add-on. Will put a config option in the onboarding checklist.

Ben — can you confirm whether we want to size the pool with 8 A100s or recommend starting with 6 active + 2 standby? I think we should present both tradeoffs to the customer.
